seoTitle: Free Terraform HCL to JSON Converter Online
metaDescription: Parse Terraform HCL2 into JSON using the Terraform JSON syntax shape, with labelled blocks nested and expressions kept as strings. Free, in browser.
intro: Parses Terraform or HCL2 configuration into JSON. Labelled blocks nest by label, unlabelled blocks become arrays, and non-literal expressions are kept as "${...}" strings, as in the Terraform JSON syntax.
why: Scripts, policy checks and documentation tools can read JSON easily, but Terraform is written in HCL. Reading .tf files from a script usually means installing a parser, and hand-converting a resource block is tedious. Paste the configuration here and get JSON in the structure Terraform itself accepts: resource.aws_instance.web style nesting, repeated unlabelled blocks as arrays, literals as values and references, function calls, conditionals and for expressions kept as "${...}" strings. Comments and heredocs are handled. Dynamic blocks are not expanded, so you see them as written. Because it parses your text locally, infrastructure code with internal names is not uploaded.
howTo: Paste your Terraform or HCL configuration into the input box.
Set the indentation of the JSON output.
Copy the JSON for your script, policy check or documentation.

faq.q: What structure does the JSON have?
faq.a: It follows the Terraform JSON syntax: labelled blocks nest by label, such as resource, then type, then name. Blocks without labels become arrays of objects.
Anything that is not a literal, such as var.region, a function call, a conditional or a for expression, is written as a "${...}" string, and is not evaluated.
No. The tool converts the syntax only and evaluates nothing, so dynamic blocks, count and for_each remain as written in the JSON and are not expanded into separate resources.

faq.q: Can I convert the JSON back to HCL?
faq.a: Yes, the YAML / JSON to Terraform HCL tool on this site writes HCL from the same JSON shape.
